original_title: Pragmata's developers take all your comparisons to Xbox 360 shooters as a 'huge compliment', though I'm not convinced by their theory for why players are making the connection
summary_en: Capcom's upcoming sci-fi adventure Pragmata is drawing comparisons to beloved Xbox 360 and PS3 era shooters. Developers are not only accepting this feedback but calling it a significant honor.

en.title: Pragmata Devs Embrace Xbox 360 Comparisons as a 'Huge Compliment'
en.summary: Capcom's upcoming sci-fi adventure Pragmata is drawing comparisons to beloved Xbox 360 and PS3 era shooters. Developers are not only accepting this feedback but calling it a significant honor.
en.body:
When **Capcom** unveiled **Pragmata**, many players immediately recognized a certain aesthetic and gameplay feel reminiscent of the golden age of third-person shooters from the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 era. Far from being offended, the development team behind the ambitious sci-fi adventure has openly embraced these comparisons, viewing them as a genuine compliment to their work.

In a recent interview, **Pragmata** director **Yonghee Cho** and producer **Naoto Oyama** shared their enthusiastic reaction to players drawing parallels to games from that formative period. Cho expressed that hearing such feedback is an honor, stating, "Honestly, it's a huge compliment. I really enjoyed games during the PS3, Xbox 360 era, and games before that era as well, so hear that it has a similar feel, that's basically an honor, a huge compliment and I appreciate the sentiment."

## A Nod to Innovation

While the developers clearly appreciate the nostalgic connection, they also offer a unique perspective on *why* these comparisons are being made. Producer **Naoto Oyama** suggests that the Xbox 360/PS3 era represented a period of significant experimentation and innovation within the gaming industry. He theorizes that **Pragmata** might be evoking that feeling because the development team itself is striving to create something new and distinct, mirroring the adventurous spirit of game development from that time. This perspective reframes the comparison not just as a stylistic echo, but as a testament to the game's own creative ambition.

## What This Means for Players

For fans eagerly awaiting **Pragmata**, this reception from the developers is a welcome sign. It suggests a team that is not only confident in their vision but also deeply connected to the history and evolution of the action game genre. The Xbox 360 and PS3 eras were pivotal for third-person shooters, introducing many mechanics and narrative styles that still influence games today. By welcoming these comparisons, **Capcom** seems to be signaling that **Pragmata** aims to capture that same sense of groundbreaking design and engaging gameplay that defined those beloved titles, while forging its own unique identity.

## What's Next

While **Pragmata** has no firm release date yet, it is slated for release on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC. Players will undoubtedly be watching closely to see how the game evolves and whether it truly captures the magic of its inspirations.

es.title: Pragmata: un homenaje a la era dorada de los disparos en tercera persona
es.summary: El juego de acción en ciencia ficción de Capcom, Pragmata, está generando comparaciones con los clásicos disparos en tercera persona de Xbox 360 y PS3. Los desarrolladores no solo aceptan estas críticas, sino que las consideran un gran honor.
es.body:
Cuando Capcom presentó Pragmata, muchos jugadores reconocieron de inmediato una estética y un estilo de juego que recordaba a la época de oro de los disparos en tercera persona de Xbox 360 y PlayStation 3. Lejos de ofenderse, el equipo de desarrollo detrás de la aventura en ciencia ficción ambiciosa ha abrazado abiertamente estas comparaciones, considerándolas un verdadero cumplido a su trabajo.

En una reciente entrevista, el director de Pragmata, Yonghee Cho, y el productor Naoto Oyama compartieron su reacción entusiasta a los jugadores que establecen paralelismos con juegos de esa época formadora. Cho expresó que oír este tipo de retroalimentación es un honor, afirmando: "Honestamente, es un gran cumplido. Me gustaban mucho los juegos de la época de PS3 y Xbox 360, y también los juegos anteriores a esa época. Escuchar que tiene un estilo similar, eso es básicamente un honor, un gran cumplido y aprecio la gesta."

## Un tributo a la innovación

Mientras los desarrolladores claramente aprecian la conexión nostálgica, también ofrecen una perspectiva única sobre *por qué* estas comparaciones están siendo hechas. El productor Naoto Oyama sugiere que la era de Xbox 360/PS3 representó un período de experimentación y innovación significativa dentro de la industria del entretenimiento. Él teoriza que Pragmata podría estar evocando ese sentimiento porque el equipo de desarrollo en sí está tratando de crear algo nuevo y distinto, reflejando el espíritu aventurero de la creación de juegos de esa época. Esta perspectiva redefine la comparación no solo como un eco estilístico, sino como un testimonio de la ambición creativa del juego.

## Lo que esto significa para los jugadores

Para los fans que están esperando ansiosos Pragmata, esta recepción de los desarrolladores es un signo acogedor. Sugiere un equipo que no solo confía en su visión, sino que también está profundamente conectado con la historia y la evolución del género de disparos en tercera persona. Las eras de Xbox 360 y PS3 fueron puntuales para los disparos en tercera persona, introduciendo muchas mecánicas y estilos narrativos que aún influyen en los juegos de hoy en día. Al acoger estas comparaciones, Capcom parece estar señalando que Pragmata busca capturar ese mismo sentido de diseño innovador y juego emocionante que definió esos títulos queridos, mientras forja su propia identidad única.

## Próximos pasos

Aunque Pragmata aún no tiene una fecha de lanzamiento fija, está programado para ser lanzado en PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S y PC. Los jugadores estarán observando de cerca para ver cómo el juego evoluciona y si realmente captura la magia de sus inspiraciones.

content_raw: If you've played Pragmata , there's a slight chance you've noticed it resembles an action game from the Xbox 360/PS3 era. By 'slight chance', I mean the connection has been made by anyone who has looked at Capcom's third-person shooter for more than five seconds. Yet while this may have been considered an insult a decade ago, today it is anything but. Not only does the similarity appear to have been a key factor in Pragmata's commercial success , its developers have been utterly thrilled by players making the comparison. In an interview with GamesRadar , Pragmata director Yonghee Cho and producer Naoto Oyama were asked how they felt about players comparing their sci-fi adventure to the golden age of third-person shooters, and apparently they began to beam even before the Japanese interpreter had finished translating the question. "The dev team has heard similar comments from both reviewers as well as players," Cho responded. "Honestly, it's a huge compliment. I really enjoyed games during the PS3, Xbox 360 era, and games before that era as well, so hear that it has a similar feel, that's basically an honour, a huge compliment and I appreciate the sentiment." What's interesting, though, is that neither developer confirms that the era of cover shooters and chainsaw bayonets was a direct inspiration. In fact, Oyama suggests that the comparison is being made because the 360/PS3 era represented a period of innovation: "Maybe the reason people might feel that way is because, during the PS3 and Xbox 360 era, a lot of different developers and publishers were experimenting with new types of games and just completely new games. Maybe that's what causes people to feel that way," he says. "Because the Pragmata dev team, as well, they put a lot of passion into creating something new." Frankly, I think it might have more to do with the fact that Oyama and Cho made a linear, single-player action game that doesn't overstay its welcome at a time when such games are vanishingly rare. Well, they were vanishingly rare until this year. 2026 has delivered a couple similar titles, like Resident Evil: Requiem and 007: First Light . Both those games have sold extremely well too, further signalling that players are hungry for the days when triple-A games were bold, brash, and (relatively) brief. Which isn't to suggest that Pragmata lacks for new ideas. Its distinctive blend of third-person shooting and hacking minigame went down well with Justin Wagner in his Pragmata Review : "It's the ace up Pragmata's sleeve that makes the whole package a winner," he wrote back in April.
